title: Kejriwal Charges BJP With Weaponizing ED and CBI
excerpt: AAP chief fires back after Enforcement Directorate raids Punjab minister Sanjeev Arora, calling it a political shakedown
body:
Arvind Kejriwal stood before cameras on Saturday, May 9, and leveled his sharpest accusation yet at the BJP-led central government: that India's top investigative agencies have become tools of partisan coercion, not anti-corruption enforcement.

**What Happened — The Trigger in Punjab:**
Kejriwal's broadside followed Enforcement Directorate raids at the residence of Punjab minister Sanjeev Arora. The ED carried out searches at five premises across Delhi, Gurugram, and Chandigarh under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with an alleged Rs 100 crore money laundering probe. This marked the second ED action at Arora's premises within a single month — the agency had previously raided his properties on April 17.

**The Core Accusation — A Pattern, Not a Case:**
Kejriwal claimed that agencies such as the ED and Central Bureau of Investigation were being used to target opposition leaders and force them to join the BJP. He pointed to what he called a telling contrast: raids were conducted simultaneously at the homes of Ashok Mittal and Sanjeev Arora, but the raids stopped after Mittal joined the BJP, while the ED returned to Arora after he refused. The BJP has repeatedly denied allegations of misusing investigative agencies, maintaining that the agencies function independently under the law.

**What to Watch — Punjab 2027 on the Horizon:**
Kejriwal vowed electoral resistance in 2027, and analysts believe the controversy may sharpen political divisions ahead of upcoming electoral battles over governance, corruption, and institutional independence.
